name: Battle of Tsushima
note: The plan shows the whole two-day action as a sketch. The accounts give courses and the order of ships, not distances, so every position is approximate. The Japanese destroyer and torpedo boat attack, said to come from the north, east and west, is drawn as one block in the north. The accounts do not say where the Japanese battleships went when they left the battleground in the evening, so they are drawn withdrawing northwards. The Russian main group included Oryol, which was later among the ships that surrendered; the plan does not follow her out of the main group.

terrain.name: Tsushima Island

units.quote: The 1st (Japanese battleship Mikasa, Shikishima, Fuji, Asahi, Kasuga, Nisshin)

units.name: Japanese 5th battle division
units.quote: The 5th battle division (Itsukushima, Matsushima, Hashidate, Chin'en) makes contact with the Baltic Fleet.

units.name: Japanese torpedo craft

units.name: Russian main group
units.quote: The Russian main group (Suvorov, Aleksandr III, Borodino and Oryol in this order)

units.quote: to cover the Left column led by Oslyabya

units.name: Nikolai I and Admiral-class
units.quote: 5th column (Left flank -West) Nikolai I, Admiral-class coastal battleship

units.quote: Transports and Auxiliaries guarded by destroyers

phases.title: The fleets sight each other
phases.text: The Russians steamed north-north-east in columns, the main group on the right, the left column and the Nikolai I group to the west and the auxiliaries behind. The Japanese main group came down from the north-east heading south-south-west.
phases.quote: The Japanese main group (Mikasa, Shikishima, Fuji, Asahi, Kasuga, Nisshin and the 2nd battle division in this order) gains visual contact.

phases.title: The Japanese turn in sequence and open fire
phases.text: Mikasa turned about and the ships behind her followed in sequence to head north-north-east. The Russian main group had shifted left to cover the left column, and the Russians opened fire on the Japanese as they turned.
phases.quote: Mikasa turns her helm aport and starts a U-turn with the 5 ships following in sequence to head NNE.

phases.title: The Japanese cross ahead of the Russian column
phases.text: Mikasa and her line turned north-east and then east to cross the T, and the Russian left column turned north-east and then east-south-east in response. Oslyabya was set on fire, and Knyaz Suvorov caught fire and fell away from the line.
phases.quote: Mikasa and her line turns NE and then to East to "cross the T". Russian Left column turns NE and to ESE in response.

phases.title: The Russian main group turns north; the Japanese reverse
phases.text: With the Japanese overtaking the Russian battleships heading east-south-east, Aleksandr III turned north with Borodino and Oryol following. The 1st division made a U-turn on the spot to head west-north-west, while the 2nd division attacked the secondary Russian warships.
phases.quote: Mikasa and the 5 ships make an immediate left U-turn on the spot, and head WNW in reverse order (Nisshin first, Mikasa last).

phases.title: The Japanese main group catches the Russian main group
phases.text: After losing sight of the Russian main group in smoke and mist, the 1st division caught up with it heading north-west and fired on the leading Aleksandr III. The 5th division, part of the 3rd Squadron, had been attacking the Russian auxiliaries.
phases.quote: Mikasa and the 1st Battle Div. catch up to the remainder of the Russian main group (heading N) in NW, and concentrate fire on the leading Aleksandr III.

phases.title: Torpedo attacks in the night
phases.text: The 1st division left the battleground and the 2nd and 4th were ordered to gather in the north, leaving the destroyers and torpedo boats to attack in the dark. The attacks forced the Russians to turn west, and they were dispersed in small groups.
phases.quote: At night, around 20:00, 21 destroyers and 45 Japanese torpedo boats were thrown against the Russians.

phases.title: The Russian remnant is surrounded and surrenders
phases.text: Tōgō's battleships surrounded Nebogatov's remaining squadron, the 1st division approaching from the north. Nebogatov signalled surrender at 10:34, and Tōgō accepted it at 10:45.
phases.quote: Tōgō's battleships proceeded to surround Nebogatov's remaining squadron south of the island of Takeshima and commenced main battery fire at 12,000 meters.
